text: On May twenty third, nineteen ninety nine, professional wrestler Owen Hart died in an accident during a live event in Kansas City, Missouri. This is a reconstruction of what happened, and why.
Owen Hart was thirty four years old. A member of the famous Hart wrestling family of Calgary, Canada, he was one of the most technically gifted performers of his era, and a husband and father of two.

That night, at Kemper Arena, Hart was to make a stunt entrance as his comedic superhero character, the Blue Blazer. The plan was to lower him from the rafters, roughly seventy eight feet above the ring, on a steel cable.

He wore a padded vest harness, clipped to the cable by a quick release snap shackle: sailing hardware, never meant to hold a person. A simpler version of the stunt had been done in November nineteen ninety eight, with a different rig. This time, just above the ring, he was to act tangled, trip the release, and fall flat on his face as a comedy bit.

But while he was still near the rafters, the shackle opened. One theory, raised by his widow, is that adjusting his cape and harness triggered it. There was no backup line. He fell about seventy eight feet, some reports say ninety, in roughly two point two seconds, reaching close to fifty miles per hour. He landed chest first on the top rope, about a foot from the turnbuckle. The impact severed his aorta.

Television viewers saw a pre recorded promo, not the fall. Medics performed C P R in the ring. He reached Truman Medical Center at seven fifty nine P M, and was pronounced dead at eight twelve, aged thirty four. After a fifteen minute pause the show continued, and about an hour later, announcer Jim Ross told viewers he had died. On November second, two thousand, the W W F settled the family's lawsuit for eighteen million dollars.

The failure had three parts. The hardware was not rated for human loads. The release could open with very little force. And there was no redundant safety line. Any live stunt needs certified equipment, professional riggers, and a backup.
His widow, Martha Hart, founded the Owen Hart Foundation in his memory. Owen Hart. Nineteen sixty five to nineteen ninety nine.
